theorem.name: Universal Triviality of Inhomogeneous Deformations of C(n+1)
theorem.statement: For all n >= 1, every inhomogeneous deformation gamma_gb of C(n+1) = osp(2|2n) is trivial (a coboundary). No constraints on the gb parameters are required.
theorem.proof_method: Explicit gauge transformation at the oscillator level
theorem.gauge_formula: a'^sigma = a^sigma + sum_j (gb_{sigma,j,-}*b_j^+ - gb_{sigma,j,+}*b_j^-) * kappa; b unchanged

gamma_formula: gamma(E_{sigma_a,j,s}, E_{sigma_b,k,t}) = gb_{sigma_b,j,s} * E_{sigma_a,k,t} + gb_{sigma_a,k,t} * E_{sigma_b,j,s}
coboundary_formula: delta_gauge(g)(X,Y) = -[X,g(Y)] + (-1)^{|X||Y|} [Y,g(X)] + g([X,Y]). This is the gauge equivalence formula for odd deformation parameter kappa, derived from Phi(X) = X + g(X)*kappa in the extended algebra.
adjoint_up_to_scalar: The 'up to scalar' condition means b_j^- b_j^+ = N_j + 1 is identified with N_j in the Lie algebra basis, since the scalar acts as zero in the adjoint representation.
